changes.before: Replace sum with function(x) x, keeping numeric(1). What happens?
changes.after: Vapply applies a function to each item and checks that each result fits a stated shape.

before:
lapply returns one list element per input element, preserving a list result even when values are simple. vapply additionally requires each function result to match an explicit length and compatible type template.

lapply receives a list and a function to call on each element. It returns a list of the function results; these two sums remain separate list elements rather than becoming the atomic vector returned by the vapply example.
```r
values <- list(c(1, 2), c(4, 5))
result <- lapply(values, sum)
cat(typeof(result), "\n", sep = "")
cat(result[[1]], result[[2]], sep = ",")
```
It prints:
```text
list
3,9
```

numeric(1) is a length-one double template here. Each sum returns one numeric total. vapply may promote compatible simpler types, but it rejects an incompatible result length or type rather than silently choosing a different output shape as sapply can.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
values <- list(c(1, 2), c(4, 5))
result <- vapply(values, sum, numeric(1))
cat(result, "\n")
```
Expected output or behavior: 3 9. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
